texts.orig: where A : [0 , ∞ ] → [0 , ∞ ] is a Young function. A function A : [0 , ∞ ] → [0 , ∞ ] is called a Young function if it is convex, left-continuous, vanishing at 0, and not constant on the entire interval (0 , ∞ ). For example, when p ∈ [1 , ∞ ), we have ‖·‖ L p ( R,µ ) = ‖·‖ L A ( R,µ ) with A ( t ) = t p , t ≥ 0. We also have ‖·‖ L ∞ ( R,µ ) = ‖·‖ L A ( R,µ ) with A ( t ) = ∞ · χ (1 , ∞ ] ( t ), t ≥ 0. Besides the classical textbooks [6, 53], the interested reader can find more information on the contemporary theory of Orlicz spaces and in particular Orlicz-Sobolev spaces in [16, 46].
